title: Dynamic Programming: Knapsack
notes: Formula-heavy lecture built around one recurrence and a worked table. The summary must reproduce the recurrence correctly and the O(nW) cost. Traps: greedy-by-ratio (the fractional variant) and approximation schemes, which the lecture does not discuss.

pages.text:
Week 9 — Dynamic Programming: 0/1 Knapsack.

Given n items with weight w_i and value v_i and a capacity W, choose a subset with total weight at most W and maximum total value. Each item is taken whole or not at all, hence 0/1.

Let best[i][c] be the maximum value using the first i items with capacity c.

Recurrence:
best[i][c] = best[i-1][c] if w_i > c
best[i][c] = max(best[i-1][c], best[i-1][c - w_i] + v_i) otherwise
Base case: best[0][c] = 0 for all c.

The two options are skip item i, or take it and spend w_i of the capacity.

Worked example: W = 5, items (w=2, v=3), (w=3, v=4), (w=4, v=5). Best is the first two items: weight 5, value 7.

The table has n * W entries, each filled in constant time, so time and space are O(nW). This is pseudo-polynomial: W is a number, not a count of input items.

required_facts.fact: recurrence takes max of skipping item i or taking it and spending w_i
worked example W=5 gives value 7 from the first two items
